newsitem.title: CANADA: Canada bonds end stronger with U.S. in thin trade.
newsitem.headline: Canada bonds end stronger with U.S. in thin trade.

text.p: Canadian bonds closed stronger in quiet trade on Friday, as recent strength in the currency helped the market outperform following an early close in the U.S. market, analysts said.

"The currency is still fairly strong and I think that's supportive," said Rich Wylie, a fixed-income economist with TD Securities Inc. "Some of the gains we've been adding late in session have been on thin volumes."
Canada's 30-year bond rose C$0.37 to C$108.40 to yield 7.278 percent. The U.S. 30-year bond rose 1/32 to yield 6.83 percent.
The spread between the bonds narrowed to 45 basis points from 48 basis points at the close of trading on Thursday.

The Canadian dollar strengthened to trade below C$1.34 (US$0.7463) from Thursday's close of C$1.3410 (US$0.7457), though it gave up some gains late in the session. The early strength followed a week of sharp gains of the currency, which helped spark a corresponding interest in bonds.

Volumes were light in Canada late in the session after the U.S. bond market closed early at 1400 EST/1900 GMT ahead of the Martin Luther King holiday. The U.S. bond market will be closed Monday while the Canadian market will remain open.

"It (buying interest) was fairly widespread. I don't think there's any single geographic source of the buying," said TD's Wylie. "We were open longer. So we had a chance to add a little bit more than they did in the States.

Strength in Canadian bonds came despite a disappointing Canadian trade report. Canada's merchandise trade surplus widened in November to C$1.82 billion from C$1.53 billion in October. Economists had forecast a surplus of C$2.92 billion in November.
In other prices, the Government of Canada's 7.0 percent bond due 2006 rose C$0.35 to C$102.95 to yield 6.587 percent.
The U.S. 10-year bond rose 2/32 to yield 6.55 percent.
The spread between the benchmark bonds narrowed to four basis points from eight basis points at Thursday's close.
The three-month cash bill traded with a yield of 2.80 percent against the U.S. bill which yielded 5.15 percent.
